newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Legal action in Indonesia church burnings soon.
newsitem.headline: Legal action in Indonesia church burnings soon.

text.p: At least 54 people are suspected of involvement in a wave of arson attacks on churches in an East Java town and legal proceedings against them will begin soon, the Jakarta Post said on Thursday.

Major General Sumarsono, chief of the East Java police, was quoted as saying that authorities had handed over dossiers of the 54 people to the prosecutor's office in Situbondo, 160 km (100 miles) east of Indonesia's second-largest city, Surabaya.
At least five people died and a courthouse and 25 churches were burned or damaged in Situbondo by a Moslem mob this month.
The riot broke out after a court hearing into a case of blasphemy against Islam.

Several thousand people outside the court demanded that the accused, a Moslem identified as Mohamad Saleh, be sentenced immediately or handed over to the crowd. The crowd went berserk after rumours spread that Saleh had escaped and taken sanctuary in a church.
Police have said 40 people have been arrested, but it was not immediately clear how many of the other 14 were also in custody.
Sumarsono was quoted as saying that some of the suspects were in their teens and have not been arrested because they were attending school.
He said a group of some 15 people was suspected to have instigated the attacks.
Police said five people, including a pastor and his wife, were burned to death in one church, while church sources said a sixth person also was killed.
About 85 percent of Indonesia's 195 million population is Moslem, although the state ideology recognises five mainstream religions and promotes religious tolerance.
